definition_zh: 剽窃；抄袭；抄袭行为；剽窃作品
definition_en: the act of presenting the words or ideas of another writer as your own
core_image: 一个人把别人论文的封面换成自己的名字
scene: 学生整段照搬网络文章却不注明出处，被导师认定为抄袭。The student copied a whole paragraph from a website without a reference and was charged with plagiarism.
sceneCN: 这里 plagiarism 是「剽窃；抄袭」（第 1 个义项：把别人的文字或观点当成自己的）；句意：学生整段照搬网络文章却不注明出处，因此被认定抄袭。

derivatives.zh: 剽窃者；抄袭者，由 plagiarism 换 -ism 为 -ist 构成
剽窃；抄袭，由 plagiarism 换 -ism 为 -ize 构成
抄袭者，由 plagiarize 加 -er 构成

senses.title: Academic theft
senses.definition: the act of presenting the words or ideas of another writer as your own
senses.definitionCN: 把另一位作者的词句或观点当成自己的东西呈现出来
senses.example: The journal rejected the paper because of clear plagiarism.
senses.exampleCN: 期刊因明显的抄袭而退回了这篇论文。
senses.why: Plagium meant kidnapping, and plagiarism carries the same image of taking what belongs to someone else.
senses.whyCN: plagium 意为拐带，plagiarism 沿用了同一意象：把属于别人的东西抱走。

senses.title: A copied piece of work
senses.titleCN: 抄袭作品；被剽窃的内容
senses.definition: a passage or a work that has been copied and passed off as original
senses.definitionCN: 被抄来并冒充原创的一段文字或一部作品
senses.example: The editor found a plagiarism of an older article in the submission.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑在来稿中发现了一段抄自旧文的文字。
senses.why: The noun can name the stolen thing itself, not only the act of stealing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指被偷走的东西本身，而不只是偷窃行为。

senses.title: Literary theft
senses.definition: the literary theft of work by another author, published under a false name
senses.definitionCN: 把他人的作品署上假名发表的文学盗用行为
senses.example: Martial mocked a plagiarist whose verses were a plagiarism of his own.
senses.exampleCN: 马提亚尔嘲笑一个抄袭者，那人的诗句其实抄自他自己的作品。
senses.why: Latin writers already used the kidnapper image for verses carried off by a rival.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁作家早已用「拐带者」的意象，指被对手抱走的诗句。

senses.title: Reuse of own work
senses.definition: the reuse of work that the same author has already published, without saying so
senses.definitionCN: 同一作者重复使用自己已发表的作品而不加说明
senses.example: Recycling an old chapter without a note is a form of self-plagiarism.
senses.exampleCN: 不加说明地重复使用旧章节，是一种自我抄袭。
senses.why: The kidnap image extends to taking from oneself, a theft that deceives readers about what is new.
senses.whyCN: 拐带意象扩展到「从自己那里拿」，这种取用会让读者误以为内容是新写的。

senses.title: Musical plagiarism
senses.definition: the use of a substantial part of music by another composer without permission or credit
senses.definitionCN: 未经许可、未给署名就使用另一位作曲家的大量音乐内容
senses.example: The band was accused of plagiarism after the melody of the single matched an old song.
senses.exampleCN: 这首单曲的旋律与一首老歌吻合，乐队因此被指抄袭。
senses.why: The same taking image applies to a melody carried over from the work of someone else.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「拿走」意象也适用于从他人作品里搬来的旋律。

intro.en: Plagiarism comes from Latin plagium, kidnapping, perhaps from plaga, a snare or net; the deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: plagiarism 来自拉丁语 plagium（拐带），可能源于 plaga（罗网、圈套），更深层的来源尚不确定。

items.en: Plagium means kidnapping, perhaps from plaga, a snare or net.
items.cn: plagium 意为拐带，可能来自 plaga（罗网、圈套）；这一词源存疑。

items.en: Plagiarius names a kidnapper of a child or a slave.
items.cn: plagiarius 指拐带他人子女或奴隶的人。

items.en: Martial applies plagiarius to a writer who steals verses.
items.cn: 马提亚尔把 plagiarius 用于偷窃诗句的写作者。

items.en: English plagiarism enters as literary theft.
items.cn: 英语 plagiarism 最初指文学盗用。

items.en: Plagiarist and plagiarize follow the noun into English.
items.cn: plagiarist 与 plagiarize 随后也进入英语。

items.en: Universities now treat plagiarism as a serious academic offence.
items.cn: 如今大学把抄袭视为严重的学术违规。

note.en: Plagiarism belongs to the Latin kidnapping family of plagiarist and plagiarize, and it sits near copying, piracy, and appropriation.
note.cn: plagiarism 属于拉丁语「拐带」词族，与 plagiarist、plagiarize 同源，并与 copying、piracy、appropriation 意义相邻。

entries.definition: to present another writer work as your own
entries.definitionCN: 剽窃；把他人作品当成自己的
复制；照抄，范围比 plagiarism 宽

entries.definition: the unauthorized reproduction of another work
entries.definitionCN: 盗版；未经授权复制他人作品

entries.definition: the taking of another culture or work for one own use
entries.definitionCN: 挪用；占用他人文化或作品，常含批评意味

normalIntro.en: Plagiarism keeps the Latin image of kidnapping: a work is carried off and given a false name.
normalIntro.cn: plagiarism 保留了拉丁语「拐带」的意象：作品被人抱走，再换上一个假名字。

normal.en: Plagiarism and plagiarius share the Latin image of kidnapping.
normal.cn: plagiarism 与 plagiarius 共享拉丁语「拐带」意象。

normal.en: A plagiarist takes the words and leaves the name behind.
normal.cn: 抄袭者拿走文字，却把原作者的署名丢下。

normal.en: Plagiarism detection compares a paper with a large database of sources.
normal.cn: 抄袭检测把论文与大型来源数据库进行比对。

normal.en: Self-plagiarism reuses old work without saying so.
normal.cn: 自我抄袭重复使用旧作而不加说明。

normal.en: Compare copying: copying can be legal, plagiarism always hides the source.
normal.cn: 对比 copying：复制可能合法，抄袭则总是隐藏来源。

abstract.en: Picture a hand slipping a page into another binder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一页纸塞进另一个活页夹。

abstract.en: Picture a book whose cover name has been scraped away.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书封面上的名字被刮掉。

abstract.en: Picture a rival carrying off a rolled scroll under one arm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个对手把一卷文稿夹在腋下带走。

examples.en: The university treats plagiarism as a breach of academic honesty.
examples.cn: 这所大学把抄袭视为对学术诚信的违背。

examples.en: She was accused of plagiarism after copying whole paragraphs from a thesis.
examples.cn: 她因整段抄用一篇论文而被指抄袭。

examples.en: A clear citation can prevent accidental plagiarism.
examples.cn: 清楚标注出处可以避免无意的抄袭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普雷杰」——雷同的杰作，其实是抄来的；谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 plagiarius（拐带他人子女或奴隶的人）→ 拉丁语 plagium（拐带）→ 英语 plagiarism，核心义「把别人的东西抱走、当成自己的」。

sensesIntro.en: Plagiarism starts as the act of taking another work, then names the stolen text, literary theft, reuse of own work, and musical borrowing.
sensesIntro.cn: plagiarism 从「拿走他人作品」的行为出发，引申为被抄的文本、文学盗用、自我抄袭与音乐抄袭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand carrying off a bound manuscript under a coat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把装订好的文稿藏在外套下带走。

branches.en: Academic theft is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 学术剽窃是核心的现代义项。

branches.en: The copied work is the result sense.
branches.cn: 被抄的作品是结果义项。

branches.en: Literary theft is the historical sense.
Reuse of own work is the self-directed sense.
branches.cn: 自我抄袭是指向自身的义项。

branches.en: Musical plagiarism is the melody sense.
branches.cn: 音乐抄袭是旋律层面的义项。

intro.en: Plagiarism is built on Latin plagium, kidnapping, with the noun ending -ism; plagiarist and plagiarize replace that ending with -ist and -ize.
intro.cn: plagiarism 建在拉丁语 plagium（拐带）之上，名词词尾 -ism 使其成为行为或现象；plagiarist 与 plagiarize 则分别换成 -ist 与 -ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin plagium means kidnapping, and plagiarius means a kidnapper, later a literary thief.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plagium 意为拐带，plagiarius 意为拐带者，后来指文学上的偷窃者。

items.meaningCN: 拐带；绑走他人子女或奴隶
items.example: Plagium gives the kidnapping image to the word.
items.exampleCN: plagium 为这个词提供「拐带」意象。

items.example: Plagiarius is the person noun behind plagiarism.
items.exampleCN: plagiarius 是 plagiarism 背后的人物名词。

items.meaning: the act of presenting another work as your own
items.example: Plagiarism turns the kidnapper into the offence.
items.exampleCN: plagiarism 把「拐带者」变成一种违规行为。

items.example: Plagiarist swaps -ism for the person suffix -ist.
items.exampleCN: plagiarist 把 -ism 换成人物后缀 -ist。

items.meaning: to present another work as your own
items.example: Plagiarize swaps -ism for the verb suffix -ize.
items.exampleCN: plagiarize 把 -ism 换成动词后缀 -ize。

items.example: Plagiarizer adds the agent suffix -er to the verb.
items.exampleCN: plagiarizer 在动词后加施事后缀 -er。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为、做法或体系的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms plagiarism from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 从拉丁词干构成 plagiarism。

items.meaningCN: 表示从事某种行为的人
表示「使……化」或「从事」的动词后缀
